title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 20
paragraphs: Then Mardonius, since the Greeks did not come down into the plain, sent against them all his cavalry, commanded by Masistios (whom the Greeks called Makistios), a man of reputation among the Persians, who had a Nesaian horse with a golden bridle and was otherwise splendidly caparisoned. When the horsemen had ridden up to the Greeks they attacked them by squadrons, and in attacking they did them much damage, and moreover in contempt they called them women.
